title: Stack of odd numbers
body: Riya is writing a Python program for her class project. The program reads integers entered by the user one at a time and pushes only the odd numbers onto a stack named oddStack, which is an ordinary Python list. She uses the list method append() for PUSH and pop() for POP, so the right end of the list is the TOP. Even numbers are ignored. After all the numbers have been entered, the program displays the contents of the stack. It then keeps popping elements until the stack is empty, and keeps the largest value retrieved so far in a variable named largest, which is set to the first popped value and updated whenever a bigger value is popped.
